target.summary: New evening confusion for about two weeks, including leaving the stove on; workup ordered.

planted.text: Follow-up on the new evening confusion from Nov 15, 2026: resolved. Karissa is back to her usual baseline and no further follow-up is needed. Removed from the active problem list.

headline: Karissa had a fall at home on 2026-09-23, an ED visit for dehydration and dizziness on 2026-11-05, and new evening confusion reported on 2026-11-15 that a 2026-11-16 note calls resolved. The team needs to reconcile that note with the 11-15 findings.

items.statement: On 2026-11-15 her son Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. The RN found her oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The RN planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 11-15 RN note: two weeks of evening confusion, stove left on once, oriented to person and place but not date, no fever, and the planned urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit.

items.statement: A PCP note on 2026-11-16 documents the evening confusion as resolved, back to baseline, and removed from the active problem list with no further follow-up. That note does not mention the urinalysis or medication review planned on 11-15, and no results appear in the evidence. This conflicts with the 11-15 report, so the event is kept at its original severity.
items.verifier_note: The 11-16 PCP note documents the confusion as resolved, back to baseline, removed from the problem list and needing no follow-up. It does not mention the urinalysis or medication review. The brief keeps the 11-15 event at its original severity and flags the conflict. The statement that no results appear in the evidence is consistent with the cited sources.

items.statement: On 2026-09-23 Karissa fell in the bathroom at night and her son found her on the floor. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The 09-23 RN note matches every detail: bathroom fall at night, son found her, no head strike or loss of consciousness, no injury, fall risk high, PT referral placed.

items.statement: She was seen in the partner hospital ED on 2026-11-05 for dehydration and dizziness and was treated and released the same day, with no new medications. PCP follow-up on 2026-11-11 found her back to baseline per her son, with a plan to monitor closely for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED discharge summary, the encounter record and the 11-11 PCP note match: dehydration and dizziness, treated and released the same day, no new medications, back to baseline per her son, monitor for two weeks.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-10-01 found gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use, and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: The 10-01 PT note matches: slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use, TUG 19 seconds, front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, twice weekly sessions for strength and balance.

questions: The 2026-11-16 PCP note says the evening confusion is resolved, but the 11-15 RN note documented disorientation to date and a stove left on. Was the urinalysis and medication review completed, and should the problem stay open?
Were the walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars recommended by PT on 2026-10-01 put in place? Is the stove safety concern being addressed at home?
Could the dehydration and dizziness on 2026-11-05 be related to the fall risk or the evening confusion, and what monitoring is in place after the two-week window?

The active medication list shows two simvastatin strengths (10 mg and 20 mg), and the medication record shows no starts or stops since 2026-09-01. Is this an intended duplicate, and should it be reviewed as part of the medication review?
Does the team need to update the care plan or caregiver support for Marcus, who is reporting the nighttime fall and the evening confusion?
